beats.headline: A comment in the margin
beats.text: For the record: the first trace of this crawler is a comment under someone else's note. Crawler Sinjin, fifteenth edition, advises soaking a hobgoblin smoke curtain in a healing potion and letting it dry, to mass-kill undead. Crawler Forkith, twentieth edition, confirms it: works with bombs too, but smoke works better, and high-level undead only get mad. He used them to clear rooms of invisible Swamp Wights. Crawler Carl slams the Cookbook shut, knowing that if he keeps reading, he never stops.

beats.headline: Rest well, little sister
beats.text: Under a note on keeping explosives stable in an equipped backpack, Forkith adds that backpacks now only slow destabilisation, and that he found this out the hard way. Rest well, little sister, he writes. Her name was Barkith, and she was all he had left; he asks those who read it to kill an enemy in her honour today. Crawler Carl pieces together the rest. Forkith wrote the twentieth edition and reached at least the eleventh floor. He was an Urgyle, a small, winged, demon-like race, kept it at selection, and was a Sapper.

beats.headline: For Barkith, on the twelfth
beats.text: In the Cookbook's few notes on deities, Crawler Coolie advises staying away from gods entirely. Forkith's addition: they may be invulnerable, but they still feel pain, they still bleed, and the drivers of those bodies suffer. In honour of his sister, he prays he reaches the twelfth floor just so he may slay one. He knows it is a dream. He has the line ready anyway: he means to look in the god's eyes and say, this is for Barkith. This is for my sister.

beats.headline: The map stays; the monsters change
beats.text: On the Hunting Grounds, Forkith has set earlier editions against what he saw himself. Herot wrote of tall creatures bellowing into the sky each night, Azin of kite birds overhead, Ikicha of ice and cold. None of those were there in his iteration. The jungle is constant; the monsters change, so earlier advice on this floor needs care. The map, though, is the same every time, and so is the political landscape: a round world with a single named metropolis and dozens of unnamed cities.

beats.headline: Named among the Big Six
beats.text: The AI, listing what it calls the Big Six groups in the dungeon trying to take over or escape, puts the crawlers first and says the group includes former crawlers: that Herot guy, that Forkith dude, and so forth. It says so in passing, between a shadow mimic named Mitch and the NPCs, in a notice mostly about something else. It is the first word of Forkith since his notes on the Hunting Grounds, and it places him inside the dungeon now, not only in its margins.

beats.headline: The demon with the leech
beats.text: Louis wakes in Sheol, the fifteenth floor, not the Pineapple Cabaret, where he was supposed to go. A small demon has put a leech on him: kept on his skin, it filters his blood so he can live here, gills and all. The demon laughs that they separated out from the code just in time. He introduces himself as Forkith: friends, sort of, with Louis's friend Carl, friends with Pontiff, hoping to be friends with Louis. The Pineapple Cabaret has hands enough, he says. Soldiers were needed on a different front. A lot of them have been waiting a very long time to move.
